tvShow.name: Star Trek: Starfleet Academy
tvShow.overview: A young group of cadets come together to pursue a common dream of hope and optimism. Under the watchful and demanding eyes of their instructors, they will discover what it takes to become Starfleet officers as they navigate blossoming friendships, explosive rivalries, first loves and a new enemy that threatens both the Academy and the Federation itself.

episodes.name: Kids These Days
episodes.overview: Caleb Mir, a brilliant street kid, is offered admission to the new Starfleet Academy class.

episodes.name: Beta Test
episodes.overview: Caleb questions whether he belongs at Starfleet Academy as the new academic year begins.

episodes.name: Vitus Reflux
episodes.overview: While our cadets compete to join an elite team at the Academy, a battle of escalating pranks breaks out between Starfleet Academy and a rival school. Tensions rise fast, threatening their newly-emerging bonds and a blossoming romance.

episodes.name: Vox in Excelso
episodes.overview: When an existential crisis threatens to wipe out a beloved but infamous Star Trek species, a cadet is forced to confront his past and strained relationship with his family. As he pursues an unexpected method of coping, Nahla races against time to save this species from extinction.

episodes.name: Series Acclimation Mil
episodes.overview: As a cadet sets out to solve an ancient Starfleet mystery, she embarks on a journey of self-discovery and learns the value of forging her own path. Meanwhile, Nahla agrees to help a fellow chancellor with an elaborate alien ritual.

episodes.name: Come, Let's Away
episodes.overview: During the cadets' first training mission on an abandoned ship, they encounter a dangerous new enemy and must fight for survival while Nahla seeks help from an unexpected source.

episodes.name: Ko'Zeine
episodes.overview: During a school holiday, cadets return home and must choose between family expectations and dreams.

episodes.name: The Life of the Stars
episodes.overview: A visiting instructor arrives at the Academy and uses an unorthodox method to help the cadets process the emotions of what it takes to become a Starfleet officer.

episodes.name: 300th Night
episodes.overview: As the year ends, Caleb must choose between the life he wanted and the life he's built at Starfleet Academy. Meanwhile, Nahla breaks protocol to keep her promise.

episodes.name: Rubincon
episodes.overview: The return of an old enemy forces Nahla to confront her own mistakes as the cadets and instructors undertake a seemingly impossible mission to save the Federation, while defining the future of Starfleet.

seasons.name: Season 1
seasons.overview: A young group of Starfleet cadets navigating friendships and rivalries, as well as first loves and a new enemy that poses a threat not to just the Academy, but to the Federation. And, in between all that drama, they strive to meet the standards of their exacting instructors.

alternativeTitles.title: Star Trek: Akademia e flotës yjore
Star Trek: Akademia e flotës yjore

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
Yes, I have to confess I came to this expecting very little and got even less. This is really just more of the woke sci fi souffle, that refuses to rise, so why not change the recipe? Based on Discovery's ratings with audiences, it's clearly not an appetising formula. 

Is there an upside? Visuals are amazing; there's no denying this is CGI at its zenith, but you can't get by on eye candy alone. Nor by recalling actors from successful series from the 1990s. Maybe there's a reason people liked those characters and series; do you think?

In summary, more of the usual woke nonsense no one asked for but definitely wants to stop. Now, I wonder how long it will take for my review to get trolled, probably by some outraged, blue-haired marketing executive?

reviews.author: hotap720
reviews.content: Really stellar entry point for modern sci-fi fans to fall in love with Star Trek. Being a younger person, I always saw Star Trek as a sort of looming force over the genre, though watching some of its old episodes (mainly of the original series) never really impressed me on account of their shoestring budget and practical effects that, at the time probably were pretty good, but looked amaeture to the modern eye used to so much flasy CGI. The old Star Trek's social commentary also didn't resonate on account of being decades in the past. But this new series really presents Star Trek in its best light, as I've seen in the first couple episodes. Compelling characters, believable relationships, intensely human and hopeful at its core that we might see a good future. And being absolutely gorgeous, musical, and giving a sense of awe and wonder at the best of times.

reviews.author: scuddzero
reviews.content: Good start to a new Star Trek series, most trek shows start with a very rocky beginning but this one aswell as strange new worlds seem to buck that trend. Was not looking forward to this show in particular after not enjoying discovery very much but was pleasantly supprised by this one and how good the characters and stories are doing so far. Not everything is perfect about it just like any other trek series I guess. But looking forward to seeing more.

reviews.author: robinm0
reviews.content:
OK, so given my age, this series is definitely not aimed at my demographic. Having watched Trek since the late 1960's, I could live with that to an extent, but the problem is, it's just not that well done either. There is a casual, one might say lack-a-daisical, feel to the whole thing, exemplified by the way Holly Hunter plays her role. She's so laid back as to be almost incoherent, affecting a 20th century hippie style which really doesn't belong here. Other characters, well, they are just there.

Then there's the script. Why are we being treated to early 21st century stereotypes, behaviour, speech and mannerisms in what is supposed to be the 32nd? 

I made it to episode 3 & gave up trying to find any redeeming features apart from the CGI, which is state-of-the-art, but the lack of proper story-telling and character development made the decision not to continue easy.
